messages.content: i want to visit my uncle by train tomorrow. i do not know when to leave.
what time do you need to get there, and do you know when a train goes there?
i need to be there before dinner. i have not found a time for the train.
first find a time for a train that can get you there before dinner.
can you just say a time?
i do not know a train time from what you said. a made up time would not help you get there.
what can i ask at the station?
which train can get me there before dinner?
i have put my clothes away, and now my room has more space.
does it feel nice to have that part done?
yes. i can sit on the chair again.
you made space to use the chair.
i do not want to clean another room today.
okay. you can stop with the work you chose for your room.
just help me say what i finished.
i put my clothes away and made more space in my room.
my book is not in my bag. ask my sister if she saw it.
did you see my book?
do not say she took it. i do not know that.
did you see my book?
add that it is the red one.
did you see my red book?
does that say she took it?
no. it asks if she saw the book, not if she took it.
this will be my first visit to that town.
is there a thing you would like to see there?
my friend said there is a little garden near the library.
you could ask your friend how to find that garden.
do you know i have been there before?
no. you said this will be your first visit.
what place did my friend tell me about?
a little garden near the library.
write that my mother reads while my father cooks.
my mother reads while my father cooks.
now use yesterday with was for both people.
my mother was reading while my father was cooking yesterday.
did my father become the person reading?
no. your mother was reading, and your father was cooking.
just the part about my father.
my father was cooking yesterday.
i want to call my grandmother. i need a quiet place where i can sit.
is there a quiet room with a chair you can use?
my bedroom has a chair, but my brother is playing music there. the kitchen is quiet and has a chair too.
the kitchen could work for the call because it is quiet and has a place to sit.
do not choose the bedroom just because of the chair.
right. you asked for both quiet and a place to sit.
just the room that has both.
the kitchen.
a woman took a coat to the park because there was wind. why did she take it?
because there was wind.
does the story say she was going to school?
no. it says she went to the park.
write both things in one sentence.
the woman took a coat to the park because there was wind.
now make it about a man.
the man took a coat to the park because there was wind.
write could you help me find my book.
could you help me find my book?
now make it please help instead.
please help me find my book.
is that still asking for help with the book?
yes. the way you ask changed, but the book is still what you want help finding.
just the please sentence again.
please help me find my book.
i plan to read at home. what if i went to the library instead?
if you went to the library, you could read there instead of at home.
i am only asking about that. i have not changed the plan.
then your plan is still to read at home.
now i want to stay with the first plan.
you can keep reading at home in your plan.
where did i choose?
at home.
my friend asked if i would like her to bring me bread. i want to say yes and thank her.
yes, please. thank you.
keep it simple. i just want yes and thank you.
yes, thank you.
now say no but keep it kind.
no, thank you.
did you say she should bring it in that last answer?
no. the last answer says no.
i have two cups on the table and plan to add two more later. how many are there now?
two cups are there now.
how many will there be if i add the two?
four cups.
i have put only one more on the table now.
then three cups are on the table now.
just how many more to reach four.
one more cup.
the bag behind the chair is my bag. the one on the table is the bag my sister has.
your bag is behind the chair.
which one should my sister take?
the one on the table.
do you know the color of each bag?
no. you said where they are, but not the color of each one.
just the place of my bag again.
behind the chair.
say my sister finished her letter with has.
my sister has finished her letter.
now make it about they.
they have finished their letter.
did you keep has with they?
no. with they, we use have.
just the last sentence again.
they have finished their letter.
we had a quiet evening at home yesterday.
what did you enjoy doing?
my brother read, and i drew a little picture.
you each had a quiet thing to do in the same room.
do we have to do the same thing to spend time together?
no. you can read and draw and still spend the evening together.
just what i did.
you drew a little picture.
ask my friend what time i have to be at her house.
what time do i have to be at your house?
now ask if i can come after lunch instead.
can i come after lunch instead?
do you know if she said yes?
no. you have not said her answer.
just the after lunch question again.
can i come after lunch instead?
i cannot go because i am tired and my shoes have water in them. write a short note.
i cannot go because i am tired and my shoes have water in them.
just keep the tired reason.
i cannot go because i am tired.
does that say my shoes have no water in them?
no. it leaves the shoes out, but it does not say there is no water in them.
just the note with one reason.
i cannot go because i am tired.
ask if the little box was opened.
was the little box opened?
now ask who opened it.
who opened the little box?
do we know someone opened it just from the first question?
no. the first question does not say someone opened it.
just the first question again.
was the little box opened?
i think my aunt may come in the morning.
you think she may come in the morning, but it is not sure.
she just said she will come in the afternoon.
now she says she will come in the afternoon.
should you still answer morning if i ask when?
no. the new answer you gave is afternoon.
just that part of the day.
afternoon.
write a sentence with the place where we met.
this is the place where we met.
now add yesterday.
this is the place where we met yesterday.
does it say which town?
no. the sentence does not name a town.
just say the day in the sentence.
yesterday.
i read a page, then i wrote a note. what did i do before writing?
you read a page.
i am drawing now. does that change what i did before the note?
no. drawing now does not change what you did before.
what am i doing right now?
drawing.
just the order of all three things.
read a page, write a note, draw.
i do not want to visit today. help me say no. i do not want to give a long reason.
sorry, i cannot visit today.
do not say i am working. i did not say that.
sorry, i cannot visit today.
add thank you for asking.
thank you for asking, but i cannot visit today.
does it give a reason i did not say?
no.
i have one book on the table and one on the shelf. how many books?
two books.
i put the table book on the shelf too.
now both books are on the shelf.
did moving it give me another book?
no. you still have two.
just the number on the table now.
zero.
i want to learn to draw a little, but i do not want a big plan.
what is one simple thing you would like to draw?
a cup on my table.
you could start with that one cup and keep it simple.
i just want one idea like that.
then the cup can be your first little drawing.
do not give me another idea, please.
okay.
ask my brother if he has been reading.
have you been reading?
now ask about yesterday with were.
were you reading yesterday?
which question has have been?
have you been reading?
just the other question.
were you reading yesterday?
i miss my sister. she is in another town.
would you like to talk about her or write her a note?
a note. ask how her day is going.
how is your day going?
do you know if she is working now?
no. you have not said what she is doing now.
just the note again.
how is your day going?
use both and with my mother and father coming home.
both my mother and father are coming home.
now make it about yesterday.
both my mother and father came home yesterday.
does both mean just one of them?
no. it says your mother and your father together here.
just the sentence about yesterday.
both my mother and father came home yesterday.
a girl went to the garden to find her toy. did she find it?
the sentence does not say. it only says why she went there.
now add that she found it under a tree.
the girl went to the garden and found her toy under a tree.
where did she find it?
under a tree.
did she find it in the house?
no. you said under a tree in the garden.
my cousin said he might visit after work. i want to ask if he is still coming.
are you still coming after work?
just ask if he is coming, not the work part.
are you still coming?
did you say he must come?
no. it is a question, not an order.
just the short question.
are you still coming?
my picture has two children sitting by a tree. write a sentence about that.
two children are sitting by a tree.
now add a little book between them.
two children are sitting by a tree with a little book between them.
did you make it three children?
no. there are still two.
just the number of children.
two.
i am going to the library now. thanks for helping with my note.
you are welcome.
i have what i need. goodbye.
goodbye. have a good visit.
